grade_rationale.text: The verified entry records Koshchei for Russians, in Afanasyev's account of Russian folk tradition and in Ralston's Russian stories.
It records him for Poles through a Polish version of the 'Sleeping Beauty' in which he puts a kingdom into a magic slumber.
Afanasyev also retells a Polish tale in which Koshchei puts others to sleep, so the Polish attestation appears in both authors.
Ralston tells the Polish tale and the Marya Morevna story without citing or quoting Afanasyev on that page, so on that passage he counts as an independent source.
Ralston's forbidden-chamber versions are footnoted to Khudyakof and Erlenvein, collectors other than Afanasyev.
Ralston's derivation of the name rests on Afanasief, whom his footnote quotes, so the etymology is counted once, not twice.
